kits.name: OPEN SOURCE STARTER
kits.summary: A minimal repository skeleton: license, contribution rules, conduct, security policy, issue and PR templates, and agent instructions.
kits.description: Start a public repository with the documents contributors and agents expect. Choose one license from this kit, then replace the placeholders in the templates.
notes: MIT is a safe default; swap in Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0, or MPL-2.0 if the project needs different terms.
Replace every placeholder before publishing.
The DCO is optional if the project uses a CLA instead.

kits.name: AGENT-READY REPO
kits.summary: Instructions, tool definitions, evaluation criteria, and contribution rules for repositories that coding agents will work in.
kits.description: Make a repository legible to coding agents without giving them uncontrolled access. The kit pairs concrete commands and boundaries with honest evaluation and disclosure rules.
notes: Fill AGENTS.md from the actual repository; do not copy commands that do not work.
Keep MCP permissions read-only unless a task requires writes.
Review the evaluation checklist before trusting an agent with releases or credentials.

kits.name: WEBSITE POLICY PACK
kits.summary: Privacy, cookies, terms, accessibility, acceptable use, DMCA, and security.txt templates for a public website or app.
kits.description: A starting pack for a small public site. Every document is a template, not legal advice; adapt it to the jurisdiction, data flows, and platform that actually apply.
notes: Remove sections that do not describe your actual data practices.
security.txt belongs at /.well-known/security.txt.
Have the final documents reviewed before relying on them.

kits.name: LICENSE PACK
kits.summary: Common license texts, source headers, and an open-source notices template in one download.
kits.description: A compact set for projects that need a license, consistent source headers, and a notices file. Pick one license; the others are included for comparison.
notes: Do not apply multiple incompatible licenses to the same code.
Keep the copyright notice and license text with every distribution.
Use the SPDX identifiers in source headers where the project supports them.

kits.name: SMALL ORGANIZATION PACK
kits.summary: Privacy, accessibility, security, conduct, acceptable use, DMCA, and issue templates for a small organization.
kits.description: A public-interest starting pack for a small nonprofit, club, cooperative, or community organization. Adapt every document to the jurisdiction and the actual data flow.
notes: Remove sections that do not describe your organization.
Have the final documents reviewed before relying on them.
security.txt belongs at /.well-known/security.txt.

kits.name: COMMUNITY GROUP PACK
kits.summary: Conduct, privacy, accessibility, security, and moderation documents for a community group.
kits.description: A starting pack for forums, local groups, online communities, and volunteer projects. Keep the rules short enough that people actually read them.
notes: State how reports are handled and who decides.
Do not publish a contact address nobody monitors.
Review the pack when the group changes platforms.

kits.name: SCHOOL PACK
kits.summary: Accessibility, privacy, open licensing, and conduct documents for a class or school project.
kits.description: A small pack for teachers, students, and school projects that publish work on the web. It includes the public-interest policies and the two most common content licenses.
notes: Check the school or district policy before publishing student work.
Do not publish personal data about minors.
CC BY requires attribution; CC0 does not.

kits.name: LIBRARY PACK
kits.summary: Public-domain, open-licensing, privacy, accessibility, and security documents for a library or archive.
kits.description: A starting pack for a small library, archive, reading room, or digitization project. It pairs rights statements with the public-interest policies a public service needs.
notes: Verify the rights status of each item before digitizing it.
Record provenance and the date of the rights decision.
Use security.txt for a monitored security contact.

kits.name: PUBLIC DOMAIN PACK
kits.summary: Public-domain dedications, the Open Source Definition, and notices for releasing work without restrictions.
kits.description: A compact pack for creators and institutions that want to release work as openly as possible. Read the difference between a public-domain dedication and a permissive license before choosing.
notes: CC0 is designed for all works; Unlicense is written for software.
A public-domain dedication may not be effective in every jurisdiction.
Keep provenance and attribution even when it is not legally required.
